title: How Forward Deployed Engineering is done at Cognition — Jia Wu

primary.label: Coding Agents & Software Engineering
primary.rationale: The talk centers on Devin, Cognition's coding agent, and its deployment in enterprise software engineering contexts. Key topics include PR throughput, code review, testing, deployment automation, and SDLC challenges. All case studies are software engineering outcomes: ETL migration at Nubank, COBOL/JCL system migration at a Latin American bank, and 10x PR acceptance rates at Built. The product surface (CLI, IDE, Devin Cloud) and internal metrics (order-of-magnitude PR increase) are squarely within the coding agent and software engineering domain.

secondary.label: Evaluation, Testing & Benchmarking
secondary.rationale: The talk presents a structured outcome measurement methodology: measuring delivery timelines before and after Devin activation (82% reduction), headcount-equivalent capacity (150%), and PR throughput (nearly doubled). Wu explicitly contrasts token-usage metrics with real delivery outcomes, advocating for delta-based measurement. This is about how quality and impact of AI systems are measured in deployed settings.

secondary.label: AI Product, UX & Human Factors
secondary.rationale: The FDE role is fundamentally about human-AI collaboration: engineers working alongside Devin, trust in the agent's outputs, and how organizations adopt and supervise coding agents. The talk discusses the T-shaped skill profile, human-in-the-loop workflows (calls plus hands-on work), and how non-technical stakeholders interact with the deployed system.

secondary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
secondary.rationale: Devin is presented as a developer platform with multiple surfaces (CLI, IDE, Cloud) deployed to enterprise engineering teams. The talk touches on the platform's evolution and how FDEs bridge platform capabilities to customer engineering workflows, though the focus is on deployment strategy rather than platform architecture.

domains.label: Coding Assistants
domains.rationale: Devin is explicitly a coding assistant and autonomous software engineering agent. The entire talk is about deploying coding agents to enterprise engineering teams and measuring their software engineering outcomes.

domains.label: Enterprise Operations
domains.rationale: All deployments are in enterprise environments: Nubank, a major Latin American bank, and Built. FDEs embed in customer engineering organizations to operationalize Devin across the SDLC, and the organizational transformation (10x for entire companies) is a core theme.

domains.label: Developer Platforms
domains.rationale: Devin is a developer tool used by engineering teams, with multiple product surfaces (CLI, IDE, Cloud). The talk discusses how this developer platform is deployed and adopted across enterprise engineering organizations.

summary: Jia Wu, Team Lead of Deployed Engineering at Cognition, presents Cognition's forward-deployed engineering (FDE) model for deploying Devin, their autonomous AI software engineer, in enterprise environments. The talk traces Devin's evolution from its 2024 SWE-bench 13.86% launch to delivering step-function improvements in PR throughput internally and parabolic enterprise adoption growth. Wu frames the FDE role as maximizing overlap between Cognition's product domain and customer problem spaces, using a two-circle model. Coding itself is described as approximately 20% of the engineering challenge; testing, reviewing, deploying, and maintaining code constitute the real problems. Deploying agents without specific direction is dismissed as "token maxing"—an era Cognition has moved beyond. FDEs embed in customer ecosystems, reviewing backlogs, remediations, delayed code, unwritten tests, and alert triage, mapping Devin to highest-leverage problems while feeding field insights back to the product roadmap. The role demands a T-shaped skill profile spanning sales engineer, solutions architect, PM, and founder personas. Three proof points anchor value: 150% headcount-equivalent capacity over 3 months, 82% delivery timeline reduction, and nearly doubled PR throughput versus single-point tools. Public case studies include Nubank (ETL migration in one-third the timeline with 50 engineers), a Latin American bank (COBOL/JCL migration at half the effort), and Built (10x PR acceptance rate). Wu closes with Cognition's core values—correctness and customer success at all costs—noting an engineer was deployed to Brazil for 10 months to ensure a customer's success, and declaring everyone at the company is go-to-market.
whyItMatters: The software engineering and AI concepts in this talk form a coherent deployment methodology for autonomous coding agents in enterprise settings. The FDE model (product-customer overlap, field-to-roadmap feedback loop, T-shaped skill profile) provides the organizational framework; the SDLC automation and capability mapping concepts define the operational workflow; outcome-based ROI measurement and session-based metrics provide the evaluation methodology; and the autonomous agent, multi-surface deployment, and AI-driven migration concepts describe the AI technology being deployed. Together, they answer how AI coding agents transition from lab benchmarks (SWE-bench 13%) to enterprise-scale delivery (82% timeline reduction, 150% headcount capacity), with the paradigm shift from token maxing to directed, outcome-measured deployment as the connecting thesis. The correctness core value ensures that throughput gains represent real engineering value rather than low-quality output volume.
temporalContext: The talk was delivered at AI Engineer World's Fair 2026 (Forward Deployed track, June 30, 2026) and published on YouTube on July 28, 2026. Research was conducted as of August 22, 2026. The talk references Devin's launch in March 2024 (SWE-bench 13.86%), internal results over the subsequent six months, enterprise adoption through mid-2026, and Cognition's release of SWE-1.7 on July 8, 2026. The 'token maxing' era is described as occurring 1-2 years prior to the talk (approximately 2024-2025), when AI budgets were subsidized and token consumption was the primary metric. The speaker, Jia Wu, became Team Lead of Deployed Engineering at Cognition in August 2025, joining through the Windsurf acquisition.
takeaways: Cognition shipped nearly an order of magnitude more robust PRs internally over six months using Devin, representing a step function increase in engineering leverage.
The industry has shifted from maximizing token usage to measuring real delivery outcomes; Cognition differentiates by making entire organizations—not just engineers—10x faster.
An 82% reduction in delivery timelines was measured by comparing agile sprint metrics before and after Devin activation within customer environments.
A 3-month embedded engagement delivered 150% headcount-equivalent engineering capacity, and PR throughput nearly doubled versus single-point tools.
Public case studies validate results: Nubank ETL migration in one-third the timeline, a Latin American bank's COBOL/JCL migration with half the effort, and Built achieving 10x PR acceptance rate.
Coding is considered a mostly solved problem; the real challenge is testing, reviewing, deploying, and maintaining code across the enterprise.
FDEs maximize the overlap between Cognition's products and customer problems, feeding field insights back to the product roadmap to de-risk future development.
Engineering challenges recur in similar shapes across companies, making each deployment derisk and improve the next.
Two core values guide all work: correctness and customer success at all costs—leaving nothing on the table.
Everyone at Cognition is go-to-market; the FDE role spans sales engineer, solutions architect, PM, and founder personas with a T-shaped skill profile.

concepts.name: Autonomous Software Engineering Agents
concepts.explanation: Devin is an autonomous AI agent that plans, writes, tests, and ships production code independently, representing a class of AI systems that operate across the full SDLC rather than just code completion.
concepts.importance: Devin is the core AI product discussed throughout the talk; its evolution from 13% SWE-bench to enterprise-scale deployment illustrates the trajectory of autonomous coding agent capabilities.

concepts.name: SWE-bench Benchmark Evaluation
concepts.explanation: SWE-bench is an automated benchmark for evaluating AI agents on real GitHub issues from Python repositories; Devin scored 13.86% at its 2024 launch (570 of 2,294 issues, 79 resolved), referenced in the talk as the starting point for Devin's capability evolution.
concepts.importance: Provides the quantitative baseline for measuring Devin's improvement trajectory and contextualizes early industry skepticism about autonomous coding agents.

concepts.name: Token Maxing vs Directed Agent Deployment
concepts.explanation: The distinction between undirected AI agent deployment that consumes tokens without producing outcomes ('token maxing') and directed deployment where agents are given specific, high-leverage tasks mapped to enterprise problems.
concepts.importance: Frames the paradigm shift in how AI coding agents should be deployed—away from raw token consumption metrics toward outcome-directed task assignment.

concepts.name: Session-Based Agent Metrics
concepts.explanation: Measuring AI agent productivity through sessions (agent execution traces) to derive productive engineering hours, rather than tracking token usage, as the basis for evaluating deployed agent performance.
concepts.importance: Introduces a concrete measurement methodology for AI agent productivity that aligns with the outcome-based measurement thesis, moving beyond input metrics to output metrics.

concepts.name: Multi-Surface AI Agent Deployment
concepts.explanation: Deploying AI agents across multiple product surfaces—CLI, IDE, and Cloud—to achieve organization-wide acceleration, contrasting with single-point tools that only accelerate individual engineers.
concepts.importance: Explains the architectural strategy behind Cognition's deployment model and why single-point AI coding tools are insufficient for organizational transformation.

concepts.name: AI Agent Capability Mapping
concepts.explanation: The systematic process of mapping AI agent capabilities to specific enterprise engineering problems (backlogs, remediations, migrations, alert triage) to identify highest-leverage deployment targets.
concepts.importance: Defines the operational methodology by which FDEs translate AI agent capabilities into enterprise value, bridging the gap between product features and customer outcomes.

concepts.name: Step Function and Parabolic AI Adoption Growth
concepts.explanation: Cognition observed step-function increases in internal PR throughput from AI agent use and parabolic growth in enterprise adoption, indicating non-linear capability and market acceleration.
concepts.importance: Characterizes the growth dynamics of AI agent adoption in enterprise settings, distinguishing incremental improvement from transformative step changes.

concepts.name: Correctness as Core Value for AI-Generated Code
concepts.explanation: Cognition prioritizes correctness—ensuring AI-generated code is robust and production-quality—as a foundational value, distinguishing from approaches that optimize for volume or speed at the expense of reliability.
concepts.importance: Establishes the quality dimension that underpins the credibility of outcome metrics; without correctness, throughput gains would not translate to real engineering value.

concepts.name: Human-AI Collaboration in Enterprise Engineering
concepts.explanation: The FDE role embodies human-AI collaboration: engineers work alongside autonomous agents, directing deployments, reviewing outputs, and providing the strategic framing that agents cannot self-generate.
concepts.importance: Frames AI agent deployment not as automation replacement but as a human-directed augmentation model, where human judgment directs AI execution.

concepts.name: AI-Driven Legacy System Modernization
concepts.explanation: Using autonomous AI agents for large-scale legacy code migration projects, including ETL migration and COBOL/JCL system modernization, demonstrating AI agent applicability beyond greenfield development.
concepts.importance: Expands the scope of AI coding agent value to enterprise modernization scenarios that are typically high-effort, high-risk, and difficult to staff, validated by public case studies.

concepts.name: Forward-Deployed Engineering (FDE)
concepts.explanation: A deployment model where engineers embed directly in customer ecosystems to maximize the overlap between product capabilities and customer problems, combining hands-on technical work with customer engagement across the full SDLC.
concepts.importance: Central organizing concept of the talk; defines how Cognition bridges its AI agent product (Devin) to enterprise engineering workflows and feeds field insights back to the product roadmap.

concepts.name: Product-Customer Overlap Model
concepts.explanation: A two-circle framing where one circle represents the product domain and the other the customer's problem space; the FDE's job is to maximize their intersection, which is where product-market fit for enterprise deployment is found.
concepts.importance: Provides the conceptual framework that guides FDEs in identifying highest-leverage deployment targets and explaining why undirected deployment fails.

concepts.name: SDLC Automation Beyond Coding
concepts.explanation: Coding is framed as roughly 20% of the software engineering challenge; the remaining 80%—testing, reviewing, deploying, and maintaining code across the SDLC—represents the real problems that FDEs target for AI agent deployment.
concepts.importance: Reframes the scope of AI agent value from code generation to full SDLC automation, explaining why single-point coding tools are insufficient for enterprise transformation.

concepts.name: Pull Request Throughput as Delivery Metric
concepts.explanation: PR throughput—the number of quality, robust pull requests shipped—is used as a primary outcome metric for measuring AI agent deployment impact, both internally and at customer sites.
concepts.importance: Provides a concrete, comparable engineering metric for evaluating AI agent ROI, replacing token-usage as the primary measurement framework.

concepts.name: Code Migration Automation
concepts.explanation: Using autonomous AI agents to execute large-scale code migration projects such as ETL migrations and legacy system (COBOL/JCL) modernization in enterprise environments.
concepts.importance: Demonstrates concrete enterprise value of AI coding agents beyond incremental productivity, validated through public case studies at Nubank and a Latin American bank.

concepts.name: Field-to-Roadmap Feedback Loop
concepts.explanation: FDEs capture high-fidelity field insights from customer deployments and route them back to the product roadmap, with the observation that engineering challenges recur in similar shapes across companies, enabling systematic de-risking of future development.
concepts.importance: Defines the second half of the FDE equation—beyond solving customer problems, feeding insights back to the product creates compounding value across deployments.

concepts.name: T-Shaped Skill Profile for Deployed Engineers
concepts.explanation: The FDE role demands broad skills across multiple domains (sales engineering, solutions architecture, product management, founder-level thinking) with deep technical spikes, contrasting with narrow specialist roles.
concepts.importance: Defines the hiring and role design philosophy that enables effective enterprise AI agent deployment, linking organizational culture to deployment success.

concepts.name: Enterprise Engineering Backlog Analysis
concepts.explanation: FDEs systematically review customer engineering backlogs including remediations, delayed code, unwritten tests, and alert triage to identify highest-leverage problems for AI agent deployment.
concepts.importance: Describes the concrete workflow by which FDEs operationalize the product-customer overlap model in practice, translating strategic framing into actionable deployment plans.

concepts.name: Outcome-Based ROI Measurement
concepts.explanation: A measurement framework that tracks delivery outcomes—timeline reduction (82%), headcount-equivalent capacity (150%), and PR throughput delta (nearly doubled)—by comparing pre-Devin and post-Devin metrics rather than token consumption.
concepts.importance: Provides the quantitative methodology for substantiating AI agent deployment value, which the speaker identifies as critical given the ambiguity of ROI measurement in the field.

concepts.name: Organization-Wide Engineering Acceleration
concepts.explanation: Cognition's differentiator is making entire organizations—not just individual engineers—10x faster, which requires multi-surface deployment (CLI, IDE, Cloud) and cannot be achieved by single-point tools.
concepts.importance: Defines the strategic ambition that distinguishes Cognition's approach from individual-productivity coding tools, framing the organizational transformation thesis.

sections.title: Introduction: Devin's evolution and product surface
sections.summary: Wu introduces himself as deployed engineering lead at Cognition, references Devin's 2024 SWE-bench 13% debut and early skepticism, and notes the product surface area includes CLI, IDE, and Devin Cloud agent. He mentions joining from Windsurf post-acquisition.

sections.title: Step function and parabolic growth from internal use
sections.summary: Cognition shipped nearly an order of magnitude more robust PRs over six months using its own agent—a step function increase. Enterprise adoption shows parabolic growth across multiple use cases, enabled by forward-deployed engineers.

sections.title: Product-customer overlap and the FDE framing
sections.summary: Wu presents a two-circle model of product domain and customer problems, with their intersection being product-market fit. FDEs maximize this overlap by deeply understanding the customer's problem space and mapping Devin's capabilities to it.

sections.title: Coding as a solved problem; token maxing vs directed deployment
sections.summary: Coding is framed as a mostly solved problem (roughly 20% of the challenge); testing, reviewing, deploying, and maintaining code are the real issues. Deploying agents without specific direction is 'token maxing.' FDEs identify highest-leverage strategic initiatives through customer calls and set up automated agent workflows.

sections.title: Embedding in customer ecosystems and the two-part equation
sections.summary: FDEs review customer backlogs, remediations, delayed code, unwritten tests, and alert triage, mapping Devin to those problems. Solving customer problems is only half the equation; feeding field insights back to product capabilities is the other half. Challenges recur in similar shapes, enabling roadmap de-risking across deployments.

sections.title: FDE personas, hiring profiles, and guiding mantras
sections.summary: The FDE role spans sales engineer, solutions architect, PM, and founder personas with a T-shaped skill profile. Cognition hires from PM, founder, and software engineering backgrounds, valuing deep spikes. Two mantras guide the work: relentless curiosity for why problems matter, and relentless customer-centricity. Wu signals a transition away from the token-maxing era.

sections.title: From token maxing to outcome measurement
sections.summary: Wu explains the industry shift from maximizing token usage (1-2 years ago, when budgets were subsidized) to measuring real delivery outcomes. The core differentiator is making entire organizations—not just individual engineers—10x faster, which single-point tools like CLIs or IDEs cannot achieve. Cognition measures sessions (agent traces) to derive productive engineering hours.

sections.title: Proof points: 150% headcount, 82% timeline reduction, doubled PRs
sections.summary: Three anonymized proof points: a 3-month embedded engagement delivering 150% headcount-equivalent capacity, an 82% reduction in delivery timelines measured before and after Devin activation, and nearly double the PR throughput versus single-point tools. Wu emphasizes measuring the delta between pre-Devin and post-Devin metrics.

sections.title: Public case studies: Nubank, Latin American bank, Built
sections.summary: Public case studies validate the results: Nubank's ETL migration with 50 engineers completed in one-third the timeline using Devin autonomously; a major Latin American bank's COBOL/JCL tax identification system migration delivered with half the required effort; Built achieved 10x PR acceptance rate and weekly output exceeding 10 engineers.

sections.title: Core values: correctness, customer success, and go-to-market for all
sections.summary: Wu closes with Cognition's core values—correctness and customer success at all costs, leaving nothing on the table. An engineer was deployed to Brazil for 10 months to ensure a customer's success. Everyone at Cognition is go-to-market because the target is making customers successful at all costs. The FDE role spans the intersection of hardest problems and software disruption at scale.

organization.name: Cognition
organization.summary: Cognition is an applied AI lab that operates Devin, the first autonomous AI software engineer. Headquartered in San Francisco, the company was founded in November 2023 by Scott Wu, Steven Hao, and Walden Yan — a team holding 10 IOI gold medals with backgrounds at Google DeepMind, Scale AI, Cursor, Lunchclub, Modal, Waymo, and Nuro. Cognition has raised over $400M from Founders Fund, Lux Capital, 8VC, and Bain Capital Ventures. As of May 2026, Cognition reported $492M run-rate revenue with enterprise usage growing >10x year-to-date. The company acquired Windsurf (agentic IDE) in July 2025, subsequently rebranded as Devin Desktop. Cognition's product suite spans Devin Cloud (autonomous cloud agent), Devin Desktop (IDE), and Devin CLI. Internally, 89% of code committed by Cognition engineers is committed by Devin. Cognition also develops proprietary software engineering models (SWE-1.6, SWE-1.7).

technologies.label: Devin Autonomous AI Software Engineer
technologies.summary: Devin is Cognition's autonomous AI software engineer that plans, writes, tests, and ships production code. The talk traces Devin's evolution from its 2024 SWE-bench 13.86% debut to delivering step-function improvements in internal PR throughput (nearly an order of magnitude over six months) and parabolic enterprise adoption growth. Devin operates across multiple surfaces (CLI, IDE/Desktop, Cloud) and is deployed in enterprise environments through the forward-deployed engineering model, achieving outcomes including 82% delivery timeline reduction, 150% headcount-equivalent capacity, and nearly doubled PR throughput versus single-point tools. Public case studies include Nubank's ETL migration completed in one-third the timeline with 50 engineers, a Latin American bank's COBOL/JCL migration at half the effort, and Built achieving 10x PR acceptance rate.
technologies.role: Core product whose enterprise deployment through forward-deployed engineering is the subject of the entire talk

technologies.label: SWE-bench Software Engineering Benchmark
technologies.summary: SWE-bench is an automated benchmark for evaluating AI agents on real GitHub issues from 12 Python repositories, comprising 2,294 instances. Devin scored 13.86% (79 of 570 issues resolved on a 25% subset) at its March 2024 launch, exceeding the previous SOTA of 1.96%. The talk references this score colloquially as '13%' or 'SweepBench 13%' to establish the starting point of Devin's capability evolution, contrasting early industry skepticism about autonomous coding agents with the current enterprise-scale deployment outcomes.
technologies.role: Referenced as the baseline benchmark for Devin's 2024 launch performance (13.86%), contextualizing its subsequent improvement to enterprise-scale delivery

technologies.label: Windsurf AI IDE (Devin Desktop)
technologies.summary: Windsurf is an AI IDE formerly known as Codeium (originally Exafunction), launched as the first agentic IDE in November 2024. Acquired by Cognition and rebranded as Devin Desktop, it serves as the IDE surface within Devin's multi-surface product architecture alongside CLI and Cloud. The speaker, Jia Wu, joined Cognition through the Windsurf acquisition path, having previously been a Deployed Engineer at Windsurf. The talk references Windsurf as part of Cognition's product surface area and uses the multi-surface architecture as a key argument for why single-point tools cannot achieve organization-wide acceleration.
technologies.role: Referenced as part of Cognition's multi-surface product strategy (CLI, IDE, Cloud) and as the speaker's entry point to Cognition through the Windsurf acquisition

technologies.label: Cursor AI Coding Agent
technologies.summary: Cursor is an AI coding agent and IDE made by Anysphere, an applied research lab founded in 2022 in San Francisco. The talk references Cursor as a representative single-point AI coding tool, arguing that such tools can only make individual engineers faster rather than entire organizations 10x faster. Cursor is contrasted with Devin's multi-surface deployment model (CLI, IDE, Cloud) as the strategic differentiator for enterprise transformation. The talk explicitly states that nearly double the PR throughput was achieved versus single-point tools, positioning Cursor and similar tools as the baseline against which Devin's organizational impact is measured.
technologies.role: Referenced as a comparison product and example of single-point AI coding tools that cannot achieve organization-wide acceleration
